questions.question: D, E, F, G, M, N and O are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table. Only E sits between N and M. M sits third to the left of O. G sits to the immediate left of O. D is not an immediate neighbour of M. Who sits third to the left of F?
questions.solution:
**Given:** D, E, F, G, M, N and O are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre of the table.

1) M sits third to the left of O.

2) G sits to the immediate left of O.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b7b763ae0b793fe2aa12cf403dabae67371bdb9a22f33bd30f79090418aaad7.png] 

3) Only E sits between N and M.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bb3ca7fe2a0f42fe525c8cf9fcfe16f2f8727a5e80fabcb95e68442c8219a505.png] 

4) D is not an immediate neighbour of M. 

After positioning D only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. F.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53f79e7ddb67a4edbb5dfbd3fd461e9f408fe55b3b7ad06b9ecd027c1929f6ed.png] 

Thus, N sits third to the left of F.

Hence, **"Option 2"** is the correct answer.

questions.question: On selling a stool for ₹8,378, the value of gain is 20% more than the value of loss incurred on selling it for ₹1,756. In order to gain 50%, find the selling price (in ₹).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total difference in **Selling Prices** = 8,378 − 1,756 = 6,622.

Ratio of **Gain** to **Loss** = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.

Sum of ratio parts = 6 + 5 = 11 units. So, 11 units = 6,622.

1 unit = 602. **Loss** (5 units) = 5 × 602 = 3,010.

**Cost Price (CP)** = 1,756 + 3,010 = 4,766.

New **SP** (50% gain) = 4,766 × 1.5 = 7,149.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,149.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → SP₁ = 8,378, SP₂ = 1,756, Gain = Loss + 20% of Loss, New Gain% = 50%.
Formulas: Gain = SP − CP | Loss = CP − SP | SP = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ae10bc2b69a14e55a6a64d9b47dc2d3c124b2d04df16d3e87440560eb99a58ba.png]

⇒ (8,378 − CP) = 1.2 × (CP − 1,756).
⇒ 8,378 − CP = 1.2CP − 2,107.2.
⇒ 2.2CP = 10,485.2.
⇒ **CP** = 4,766.
⇒ New **SP** = 4,766 + (50% of 4,766) = 4,766 + 2,383 = 7,149.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,149.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Relationship

questions.question: Two positive numbers differ by 2134. When the greater number is divided by the smaller number, the quotient is 2 and the remainder is 147. What is the HCF of the greater of the two given numbers and 4225?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **smaller number** be x and **greater number** be y.

Given: y − x = 2134 and y = 2x + 147.

Substitute y: (2x + 147) − x = 2134 ⇒ x = 2134 − 147 = 1987.

Greater number y = 1987 + 2134 = 4121.

HCF(4121, 4225) → Difference = 4225 − 4121 = 104. Factors of 104 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 13, 26, 52, 104. Testing 13: 4121 ÷ 13 = 317.

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f988af0e02532cd634ab2deb556107683a0626f5d34b87fd59634569a03f0d1.png] 

**Given:**

Difference (y − x) = 2134

Division rule: **Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder**

⇒ y = (x × 2) + 147

⇒ y = 2x + 147

**Calculations:**

⇒ (2x + 147) − x = 2134

⇒ x + 147 = 2134

⇒ x = 1987

⇒ y = 1987 + 2134 = 4121

Now, find **HCF of 4121 and 4225**:

⇒ 4225 = 4121 × 1 + 104

⇒ 4121 = 104 × 39 + 65

⇒ 104 = 65 × 1 + 39

⇒ 65 = 39 × 1 + 26

⇒ 39 = 26 × 1 + 13

⇒ 26 = 13 × 2 + 0

**∴ The correct answer is 13.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Euclid's Division Lemma

For any two positive integers a and b, there exist unique integers q and r such that a = bq + r, where 0 ≤ r < b.

HCF by Difference Method

The HCF of two numbers also divides their difference. This is useful for finding HCF of large numbers quickly.

Properties of HCF

HCF(a, b) = HCF(a, b − a). If a number k divides both a and b, then k must divide the HCF of a and b.</p

questions.question: A rectangular tin sheet is 32 cm long and 14 cm wide. It is rolled along its length to form a cylinder, with opposite edges just touching each other. Find the volume (in cm³) of the cylinder.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a **rectangular sheet** is rolled along its **length**, the **length** becomes the **circumference** (2πr) and the **width** becomes the **height** (h).

Circumference 2πr = 32 ⇒ r = 16/π

Volume V = πr²h = π × (16/π)² × 14

V = π × (256/π²) × 14 = (256 × 14)/π = 3584/π

**∴ The correct answer is 3584/π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length** of sheet (L) = 32 cm

**Width** of sheet (W) = 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

**Circumference** of circle = 2πr

**Volume** of cylinder = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d5c278d6752584d6569904a9f247f298599fbffbbd871ce2d232933d707333ea.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ When rolled along the length, **Circumference** = 32 cm

⇒ 2 × π × r = 32

⇒ r = 32 / (2π) = 16/π cm

⇒ **Height** of the cylinder (h) = Width of the sheet = 14 cm

⇒ **Volume** (V) = π × r² × h

⇒ V = π × (16/π)² × 14

⇒ V = π × (256 / π²) × 14

⇒ V = (256 × 14) / π

⇒ V = 3584/π cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 3584/π cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cylinder Rolling (Along Width)

If the sheet is rolled along its width, the **width** becomes the **circumference** (2πr = W) and the **length** becomes the **height** (h = L).

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The CSA of the resulting cylinder is always equal to the **Area of the Rectangular Sheet** (L × W), which is 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The TSA of a solid cylinder includes the top and bottom circles: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r).</p

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India prevents any child below the age of 14 years from being employed in the factory, mine or hazardous occupation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 24**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 24** of the Constitution of India prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or any hazardous occupations.
 
• This provision is part of the fundamental rights under the **Right against Exploitation** outlined in the Constitution.
 
• The article aims to protect children from exploitation and hazardous working conditions that can harm their physical and mental health.
 
• It aligns with the government's commitment to ensuring the welfare and development of children by preventing child labor in unsafe environments.
 
• India has ratified international conventions such as the **UN Convention on the Rights of the Child** and the **ILO Convention No. 182** to combat child labor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Labor Prohibition and Regulation Act, 1986:**

 
 
• This act regulates the working conditions for children and prohibits their employment in hazardous occupations.
 
• It defines hazardous occupations and processes where child labor is strictly prohibited.
 
 
 
• **The Right to Education Act, 2009:**
 
 
• This act ensures free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years, thereby indirectly combating child labor.
 
• Education is seen as a key tool to prevent children from being exploited in the workforce.
 
 
 
• **National Child Labor Project (NCLP):**
 
 
• Under this initiative, children withdrawn from hazardous work are enrolled in special schools to provide education, nutrition, and vocational training.
 
• The program aims to rehabilitate child laborers and integrate them into the mainstream education system.
 
 
 
• **International Initiatives:**
 
 
• India is a signatory to the **ILO Minimum Age Convention (No. 138)**, which sets the minimum age for employment.
 
• The **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** also emphasize the elimination of child labor under Goal 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth).

questions.question: A person who spends 50% of his monthly income is able to save ₹7,056 per month. His monthly expenses (in ₹) are:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the person spends **50%** of his **monthly income**, his savings percentage is also **50%** (100% − 50%).

When **Expenditure % = Savings %**, then the **Expenditure value = Savings value**.

Given **Savings** = ₹7,056.

Therefore, **Monthly Expenses** = ₹7,056.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,056.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Monthly Savings** = ₹7,056

**Expenditure Percentage** = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Savings % = 100% − Expenditure %

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d61554f6a555472c1664979f89137188682a6adcc39d39a492ee8fe87395db3f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Savings %** = 100% − 50% = 50%

⇒ 50% of **Income** = ₹7,056

⇒ **Monthly Expenses** = 50% of **Income**

⇒ **Monthly Expenses** = ₹7,056

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,056.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income-Expenditure Relation

Total Income is always the sum of Expenditure and Savings. **Income = Expenditure + Savings**.

Percentage Change

If income increases by x% and expenditure increases by y%, the change in savings depends on the initial ratio of expenditure to savings.

Base Value

In income-based problems, the **Total Income** is generally treated as the base value (100%) for calculating percentages of spending or saving.

questions.question: The 'Drain of Wealth' theory, which highlighted the economic exploitation of India under British rule, was prominently advocated by whom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dadabhai Naoroji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji was an Indian political leader, educator, and economist who is famously known as the **'Grand Old Man of India.'**
 
• He introduced the 'Drain of Wealth' theory in his book **"Poverty and Un-British Rule in India,"** published in 1901.
 
• The theory highlighted how the British systematically drained India's wealth and resources for their economic benefit.
 
• Naoroji was the first Indian to become a member of the British Parliament, where he actively raised concerns about the economic exploitation of India.
 
• The 'Drain of Wealth' theory became a cornerstone for the Indian freedom movement, influencing leaders like Mahatma Gandhi and Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Key Aspects of the 'Drain of Wealth' Theory:**

 
 
• The theory argued that a significant portion of India's wealth was being transferred to Britain in the form of **home charges** (administrative expenses and pensions).
 
• Export of raw materials and the import of finished goods from Britain created a massive trade imbalance.
 
• Indian taxpayers funded the salaries and pensions of British officials, further depleting the country's resources.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Theory:**
 
 
• The theory exposed the economic exploitation of India under British rule, fueling nationalist sentiments.
 
• It provided a strong economic argument for independence and self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Dadabhai Naoroji's Other Contributions:**
 
 
• He co-founded the **Indian National Congress (INC)** in 1885, which later became the primary political platform for India's independence struggle.
 
• He was the first Indian to be elected to the British House of Commons in 1892 as a Liberal Party candidate.
 
 
 
• **Other Advocates of Economic Nationalism:**
 
 
• While Naoroji introduced the 'Drain of Wealth' theory, other leaders like Gopal Krishna Gokhale and R.C. Dutt also highlighted the economic impact of British policies.

questions.question: In October 2024, the Mediation Act, 2023 came into force. What is a key feature introduced by this legislation?

options.text: It replaces arbitration and conciliation with mediation as the sole dispute resolution method.
It mandates that all mediation proceedings must be conducted only by retired judges.
It abolishes the role of mediators in public sector disputes.
It makes mediation compulsory for all civil and commercial disputes before court proceedings.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It makes mediation compulsory for all civil and commercial disputes before court proceedings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Mediation Act, 2023 introduces **mandatory pre-litigation mediation** for civil and commercial disputes, aiming to reduce the burden on courts.
 
• This legislation promotes a **time-bound dispute resolution mechanism**, ensuring faster settlements through mediation.
 
• The Act establishes a **Mediation Council of India** to regulate the conduct of mediators and mediation institutions.
 
• It provides legal recognition to **mediated settlement agreements**, making them enforceable as court decrees.
 
• The Act encourages participation of trained mediators, ensuring professional and impartial facilitation in dispute resolution processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mediation:**

 
 
• Mediation is a voluntary and collaborative process where disputing parties work with a neutral third party (mediator) to resolve their issues.
 
• It differs from arbitration as it does not involve binding decisions made by a third party.
 
 
 
• **Mediation Council of India:**
 
 
• Established under the Mediation Act, 2023, the council oversees the accreditation of mediators and mediation service providers.
 
• It aims to standardize mediation practices across India.
 
 
 
• **Mediated Settlement Agreements:**
 
 
• These agreements, reached through mediation, carry legal enforceability under the Act.
 
• They are treated as final and binding, similar to court decrees.
 
 
 
• **Pre-litigation Mediation:**
 
 
• This process requires disputing parties to attempt mediation before approaching the court.
 
• It helps in reducing litigation costs and court congestion.

questions.question: Which version of Windows introduced the Start menu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Windows 95**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Windows 95** was the first version of the Windows operating system to introduce the Start menu, a revolutionary feature for navigation.
 
• The Start menu combined the list of installed programs with quick access to system settings, making it user-friendly and efficient.
 
• It was launched on **August 24, 1995**, and marked a significant shift towards graphical user interfaces (GUI).
 
• The Start button, located at the bottom-left corner of the screen, became a hallmark of Windows operating systems.
 
• This version also introduced other innovations like the taskbar, long file names, and built-in support for plug-and-play hardware.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Windows is a family of operating systems developed by Microsoft, designed for personal computers, tablets, and embedded systems.
 
• It is one of the most widely used operating systems globally, with billions of active installations.
 
 
 
• **Graphical User Interface (GUI):**
 
 
• The GUI allows users to interact with electronic devices through visual indicators like icons and buttons instead of text-based interfaces.
 
• Windows 95 was a major step forward in popularizing GUI for mainstream computer users.
 
 
 
• **Taskbar:**
 
 
• The taskbar, introduced in Windows 95, allows users to see and switch between open applications easily.
 
• It is located at the bottom of the screen and includes the Start button, quick launch icons, and the system clock.
 
 
 
• **Plug and Play (PnP):**
 
 
• Windows 95 introduced built-in support for PnP, allowing hardware devices to be automatically recognized and configured by the operating system.
 
• This feature greatly simplified the process of adding new hardware to a computer.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Start Menu:**
 
 
• The Start menu became an iconic feature of Windows, evolving through subsequent versions like Windows XP, Windows 7, and Windows 10.
 
• It remains a central element for accessing applications and settings in modern Windows systems.

questions.question: Simplify: (3z − 9y)² + (9z + 3y)² − 81z²
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Observe that in (3z − 9y)² and (9z + 3y)², the **middle terms** are −2(3z)(9y) = −54zy and +2(9z)(3y) = +54zy.

These terms **cancel** each other out when added.

Remaining terms: (3z)² + (9y)² + (9z)² + (3y)² − 81z²

⇒ 9z² + 81y² + 81z² + 9y² − 81z² = 9z² + 90y²

**∴ The correct answer is 9z² + 90y².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (3z − 9y)² + (9z + 3y)² − 81z²

**Formula Used:** (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² and (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²

⇒ (3z − 9y)² = (3z)² − 2 × 3z × 9y + (9y)² = 9z² − 54zy + 81y²

⇒ (9z + 3y)² = (9z)² + 2 × 9z × 3y + (3y)² = 81z² + 54zy + 9y²

⇒ Adding both expansions: (9z² − 54zy + 81y²) + (81z² + 54zy + 9y²) = 90z² + 90y²

⇒ Final simplification: 90z² + 90y² − 81z²

⇒ (90z² − 81z²) + 90y² = 9z² + 90y²

**∴ The correct answer is 9z² + 90y².**

**__Additional Information__**

Binomial Square Identities

The identities (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b² are fundamental **algebraic identities** used to expand squared binomials.

Combining Like Terms

Terms that have the same **variable** and **exponent** (like 9z² and 81z²) can be added or subtracted by operating on their coefficients.

Sum of Squared Binomials

If the terms are identical, (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²). In this problem, while terms differed, the **middle terms** still canceled due to the structure 2(3z)(9y) = 2(9z)(3y).</p

questions.question: If 20% of k is 10 less than 1200% of 10, then k is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **percentages** to decimals: 20% = 0.2 and 1200% = 12.

The equation becomes: 0.2 × k = (12 × 10) − 10

0.2k = 120 − 10 = 110

k = 110 ÷ 0.2 = 1100 ÷ 2 = 550

**∴ The correct answer is 550.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 20% of k = (1200% of 10) − 10

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b2aeef2ffe120a94d5dc9f7d10b99db04149ac21a12397288c90b21adb0263b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 20/100 × k = (1200/100 × 10) − 10

⇒ 1/5 × k = (12 × 10) − 10

⇒ k/5 = 120 − 10

⇒ k/5 = 110

⇒ k = 110 × 5

⇒ k = 550

**∴ The correct answer is 550.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert x% to a fraction, divide by 100: x/100. For example, 1200% = 1200/100 = 12.

Percentage Change Formula

Percentage change = [(New Value − Original Value) ÷ Original Value] × 100.

A% of B property

questions.question: What type of majority is required to pass laws under Articles 2 and 3, as per Article 4(2) in Indian parliament?

• Unlike constitutional amendments (which often require special or two-thirds majorities), these laws are considered ordinary legislation.
 
• This provision ensures flexibility in reorganizing states to address administrative and political needs.

• It excludes abstentions and absent members from the total count.
 
 
 
• **Special Majority:**
 
 
• A special majority requires a higher threshold, such as two-thirds of the members present and voting, or in some cases, two-thirds of the total membership of the house.
 
• It is typically required for constitutional amendment bills under Article 368.
 
 
 
• **State Reorganization:**
 
 
• State reorganization involves altering the boundaries, names, or areas of states to address linguistic, cultural, or administrative concerns.
 
• Examples include the formation of Telangana in 2014 and the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh.

• Article 3 enables the reorganization of states through changes in boundaries, areas, and names.
 
 
 
• **Article 4(2):**

• Thus, they can be enacted through a simple majority, unlike constitutional amendment bills.

questions.question: Gopal bought 51 books at ₹1,120 per book from one shop and 45 books at ₹920 per book from another. What is the average price (in ₹) he paid per book?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **assumed average** be **₹1,000**.

Deviation of Group 1 (51 books): 51 × (+120) = **+6,120**

Deviation of Group 2 (45 books): 45 × (−80) = **−3,600**

Net deviation = 6,120 − 3,600 = **+2,520**

Average deviation = 2,520 ÷ (51 + 45) = 2,520 ÷ 96 = **26.25**

Actual Average = 1,000 + 26.25 = **1,026.25**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,026.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quantity of books from **Shop 1** (n₁) = **51** | Price (p₁) = **₹1,120**

Quantity of books from **Shop 2** (n₂) = **45** | Price (p₂) = **₹920**

**Formula Used:**

**Average Price** = (Total Cost) ÷ (Total Quantity)

Average = (n₁p₁ + n₂p₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a59bd7b6527bb340092def3beba05dc9b0b7dfa69d6d6a544d2406234a9cb30.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total cost from Shop 1 = 51 × 1,120 = **₹57,120**

⇒ Total cost from Shop 2 = 45 × 920 = **₹41,400**

⇒ Total cost of all books = 57,120 + 41,400 = **₹98,520**

⇒ Total number of books = 51 + 45 = **96**

⇒ Average price = 98,520 ÷ 96

⇒ Average price = **₹1,026.25**

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,026.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

It is the average where each observation is assigned a **weight** based on its importance or quantity. Formula: Aw = Σ(wᵢ × xᵢ) ÷ Σwᵢ.

Deviation Method for Averages

Instead of multiplying large numbers, assume a **mean** and calculate the **algebraic sum** of differences from that mean to find the correction.

Average Speed and Price Relationship

Average price/speed is not just the **arithmetic mean** of the individual prices/speeds unless the **quantities/times** are equal.

questions.question: Which bacterial disease is specifically confirmed by a serological method?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Typhoid**__.

*__Key Points__

__
 
• **Typhoid** is a bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi*, which spreads through contaminated food and water.
 
• The disease is commonly diagnosed using the **Widal test**, a serological test that detects antibodies against *S. typhi* antigens.
 
• The Widal test evaluates the presence of **O (somatic) and H (flagellar) antigens** in the blood, which are specific to typhoid fever.
 
• This method is preferred in areas with limited access to advanced diagnostic tools and is widely used for diagnosing typhoid in endemic regions.
 
• While the Widal test is widely used, its results must be interpreted cautiously alongside the patient’s clinical history and other diagnostic findings.

***Additional Information__**

 
• **Widal Test:**

 
 
• Developed in 1896 by Georges-Fernand Widal, it remains one of the most common methods to diagnose typhoid fever.
 
• A fourfold increase in antibody titers in two consecutive samples taken 7–10 days apart confirms the diagnosis of typhoid.
 
• False-positive results may occur due to previous infections or vaccination with S. typhi*.
 
 
 
• **Other Diagnostic Methods for Typhoid:**
 
 
• Blood Culture: The most reliable method, especially in the early stages of the disease.
 
• Bone Marrow Culture: Considered the most sensitive diagnostic method but is invasive and rarely used.
 
• Typhidot Test: A rapid diagnostic test that detects IgM and IgG antibodies specific to typhoid.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms of Typhoid:**
 
 
• High fever, abdominal pain, weakness, headache, loss of appetite, and constipation or diarrhea.
 
• In severe cases, it can lead to intestinal perforation and sepsis.
 
 
 
• **Prevention of Typhoid:**
 
 
• Vaccination: Typhoid conjugate vaccines and oral live-attenuated vaccines are available.
 
• Ensure safe drinking water, proper sanitation, and hygiene to prevent transmission.

questions.question: What is the third proportional of 2x² and 12xy?

For two numbers **a** and **b**, the **third proportional** (c) is calculated as **b² / a**.

Third Proportional = (12xy)² ÷ 2x²

⇒ (144x²y²) ÷ 2x² = 72y²

**Given:**

First term (a) = **2x²**

Second term (b) = **12xy**

If a, b, and c are in **continued proportion**, then **a : b = b : c**, where c is the **third proportional**.

⇒ a / b = b / c

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2x² / 12xy = 12xy / c

⇒ c = (12xy × 12xy) / 2x²

⇒ c = 144x²y² / 2x²

⇒ c = 72y²

**∴ The correct answer is 72y².**

**__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers **a** and **b** is given by **√(ab)**.

Fourth Proportional

For three numbers **a**, **b**, and **c**, the fourth proportional **d** is given by **(b × c) / a** such that a : b = c : d.

Continued Proportion

Three quantities **a, b, c** are in continued proportion if the ratio of the first to the second is equal to the ratio of the second to the third (**a:b = b:c**).</p

questions.question: {If } sin⁴theta - cos⁴theta = (1)/(2), { find the value of } 2sin²theta - 1.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ = 1/2**.

Using **a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)**, we get (sin²θ − cos²θ)(sin²θ + cos²θ) = 1/2.

Since **sin²θ + cos²θ = 1**, the expression becomes **sin²θ − cos²θ = 1/2**.

We know that **cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ**, so sin²θ − (1 − sin²θ) = **2sin²θ − 1 = 1/2**.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0fd49775feb3e49562a6c6bfd688289a2f158cc3ba5f2bbc68dcfe0784de487e.png] 

**Given:** sin⁴θ − cos⁴θ = 1/2

**Formula Used:** a⁴ − b⁴ = (a² − b²)(a² + b²) and sin²θ + cos²θ = 1

⇒ (sin²θ)² − (cos²θ)² = 1/2

⇒ (sin²θ − cos²θ)(sin²θ + cos²θ) = 1/2

⇒ (sin²θ − cos²θ) × 1 = 1/2

⇒ sin²θ − (1 − sin²θ) = 1/2

⇒ sin²θ − 1 + sin²θ = 1/2

⇒ 2sin²θ − 1 = 1/2

**∴ The correct answer is 1/2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identity

The fundamental identity is sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, which can be rearranged as cos²θ = 1 − sin²θ or sin²θ = 1 − cos²θ.

Double Angle Formulas

cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ = 1 − 2sin²θ = 2cos²θ − 1. In this problem, 2sin²θ − 1 is equivalent to −cos 2θ.</p

questions.question: The product of two consecutive positive integers is 247. If the smaller of these two integers is represented by x, which of the following will correspond to the equation for finding out the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **smaller integer** be x and the next **consecutive integer** be x + 1.

The **product** is given as x × (x + 1) = 247.

Expanding the bracket: x² + x = 247.

Rearranging into **standard quadratic form**: x² + x − 247 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is x² + x − 247 = 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Smaller integer = x

Product of **two consecutive positive integers** = 247

**Calculation:**

Since the integers are **consecutive**, the second integer must be (x + 1).

According to the problem, the **product** of these integers is 247.

⇒ x × (x + 1) = 247

⇒ x(x) + x(1) = 247

⇒ x² + x = 247

To form the **quadratic equation**, move all terms to the left side:

⇒ x² + x − 247 = 0

This equation represents the relationship used to find the value of the **smaller integer** x.

**∴ The correct answer is x² + x − 247 = 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Integers

Integers that follow each other in order without gaps. If the first is n, the next is n + 1, followed by n + 2, and so on.

Quadratic Equation Standard Form

A quadratic equation is typically written in the form ax² + bx + c = 0, where a ≠ 0.

Consecutive Even or Odd Integers

If the integers are specified as even or odd, the difference between them is 2, represented as x and x + 2.

Nature of Roots

For the equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the discriminant D = b² − 4ac determines if roots are real, equal, or imaginary.</p

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a dimension measured by the Gender Inequality Index (GII)?

• **Labor market participation** is assessed by the labor force participation rate of women compared to men.

• Maternal mortality ratio: The number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births.

• This reduction is often aimed at encouraging borrowing and investment to stimulate economic growth.

• The repo rate decision is a balance between supporting growth and ensuring price stability.

• The Central Highlands are bounded by the **Aravalli Hills in the northwest** and the Vindhyan Range to the south.

questions.question: Mohan invested ₹1,320 at 6% per annum simple interest in a bank. What amount (in ₹) will he get after 6 years?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage = **Rate × Time** = 6% × 6 = 36%.

Total amount percentage = 100% + 36% = 136%.

Amount = 1320 × 136% = 1320 × 1.36 = ₹1,795.2.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,795.2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹1,320

Rate (R) = 6% per annum

Time (T) = 6 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Total Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ac81b04a9d7e7ae8ff5292e7f1b184f284d89226887a97e16bad90c4a8ffc992.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (1320 × 6 × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (1320 × 36) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 47520 ÷ 100 = ₹475.2

⇒ Total Amount = 1320 + 475.2

⇒ Total Amount = ₹1,795.2

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,795.2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Direct Amount Formula (SI)

The final amount can be calculated directly using A = P(1 + RT/100).

Relationship between Interest and Time

In **Simple Interest**, the interest earned remains constant every year if the principal and rate are unchanged.

SI vs CI Difference

For the first year, **Simple Interest** and **Compound Interest** are identical if the interest is compounded annually.

questions.question: A cistern has a hole in the bottom through which the water is leaking. A tap can fill the cistern in 6 hours and the hole in the bottom can empty the fully filled cistern in 15 hours. If both the tap and the hole are open, then what will be the time taken to completely fill the empty cistern?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net filling time = (**a × b**) ÷ (**b − a**), where a = filling time and b = emptying time.

Net filling time = (**6 × 15**) ÷ (**15 − 6**)

Net filling time = **90 ÷ 9** = **10 hours**.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **Tap (A)** to fill = **6 hours**

Time taken by **Hole (B)** to empty = **15 hours**

 **Source**
 **Time (hr)**
 **Total Capacity (LCM)**
 **Efficiency**

 **Tap (A)**
 6
 30 units
 +5

 **Hole (B)**
 15
 −2

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Capacity** = LCM(6, 15) = **30 units**

⇒ **Efficiency of Tap (A)** = 30 ÷ 6 = **+5 units/hr**

⇒ **Efficiency of Hole (B)** = 30 ÷ 15 = **−2 units/hr**

⇒ **Combined Efficiency (A + B)** = 5 − 2 = **3 units/hr**

⇒ **Time taken to fill the cistern** = Total Capacity ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ **Time** = 30 ÷ 3 = **10 hours**

**∴ The correct answer is 10 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An **inlet pipe** fills the tank (positive efficiency), while an **outlet pipe** (or leak) empties the tank (negative efficiency).

Net Work Done

If 1/x is the filling rate and 1/y is the emptying rate, net work per hour = **1/x − 1/y** (when filling is faster).

Pipes & Cisterns Analogy

This concept is identical to **Time & Work**, where filling is **positive work** and emptying/leaking is **negative work**.</p

questions.question: If the eight-digit number 43377p08 is divisible by 8, then the maximum value of p is:

For a number to be **divisible by 8**, its **last three digits** must be divisible by 8.

Last three digits of **43377p08** are **p08**.

Checking the **maximum value** of **p** from the options: **p = 8**.

The number **808** is divisible by 8 (808 ÷ 8 = 101).

**∴ The correct answer is 8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** An eight-digit number **43377p08** is divisible by 8.

**Divisibility Rule of 8:** A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its **last three digits** is divisible by 8.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d474d981a375d00253f3d06380fe73f224d2ffa9912090597758f1f29737c3ad.png] 

⇒ Last three digits = **p08**

⇒ If p = 9, 908 ÷ 8 ⇒ Remainder = 4 (Not divisible)

⇒ If **p = 8**, 808 ÷ 8 = 101 (Divisible)

questions.question: For what values of b, the quadratic equation 4x² + bx + 16 = 0 has equal real roots?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a **quadratic equation** ax² + bx + c = 0 to have **equal real roots**, the value of b is given by ±2√(ac).

⇒ b = ±2 √(4 × 16)

⇒ b = ±2 √64

⇒ b = ±2 × 8 = ±16

**∴ The correct answer is 16 and −16.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The **quadratic equation** is 4x² + bx + 16 = 0.

**Formula Used:** For **equal real roots**, the **discriminant (D)** of the equation ax² + bx + c = 0 must be zero.

D = b² − 4ac = 0

**Calculations:**

⇒ Comparing 4x² + bx + 16 = 0 with ax² + bx + c = 0, we get:

⇒ a = 4, b = b, c = 16

⇒ D = b² − 4 × 4 × 16 = 0

⇒ b² − 256 = 0

⇒ b² = 256

⇒ b = √256

⇒ b = 16 or b = −16

**∴ The correct answer is 16 and −16.**

**__Additional Information__**

Nature of Roots

The **discriminant** D = b² − 4ac determines the nature: if D > 0, roots are **real and distinct**; if D = 0, roots are **real and equal**; if D < 0, roots are **imaginary**.

Sum and Product of Roots

For a **quadratic equation**, the **sum of roots** is −b/a and the **product of roots** is c/a.

Perfect Square Condition

A **quadratic expression** is a **perfect square** if and only if its **discriminant** is zero, which results in **equal roots**.</p

questions.question: In Windows OS, which of the following actions will permanently delete a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin?

__
 
• Pressing **Shift + Delete** bypasses the Recycle Bin and permanently deletes a file from the system.

• The **Recycle Bin** is a feature in Windows OS that stores deleted files temporarily until manually cleared.
 
• Files deleted using **Shift + Delete** cannot be restored through the Recycle Bin.
 
• For accidental permanent deletion, specialized data recovery software may be required to retrieve the file.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Recycle Bin in Windows OS**

 
 
• The Recycle Bin is a special folder where deleted files are temporarily stored.
 
• Users can restore files from the Recycle Bin unless the bin has been emptied or files are deleted permanently using Shift + Delete.
 
• The Recycle Bin can be customized to allocate a specific amount of storage space for deleted files.
 
 
 
• **Permanent Deletion**
 
 
• Permanent deletion bypasses temporary storage locations like the Recycle Bin.
 
• It removes file references from the file system, but the actual data remains on the storage device until overwritten.
 
• Tools like disk shredders can be used to overwrite deleted files, ensuring complete erasure.
 
 
 
• **Data Recovery**
 
 
• Data recovery tools like EaseUS or Recuva can retrieve files that have been deleted permanently, provided the data has not been overwritten.
 
• Recovery is more successful if attempted promptly after deletion.
 
 
 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts in Windows**
 
 
• Shift + Delete: Permanently deletes a file without sending it to the Recycle Bin.

• Alt + Tab: Switch between open windows.

questions.question: How much will a sum of ₹72,000 become after one year if the interest is compounded half-yearly at 10% per annum compound interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For **half-yearly compounding**, the rate becomes half (5%) and time periods double (2 periods).

Effective interest rate for 2 periods at 5% = 5 + 5 + (5 × 5)/100 = **10.25%**.

Total Amount = 110.25% of **₹72,000**.

⇒ Amount = 72,000 × 1.1025 = **₹79,380**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹79,380.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Principal (P) = ₹72,000, Rate (R) = 10% p.a., Time (T) = 1 year.

Since the interest is compounded **half-yearly**:

⇒ New Rate (r) = 10% ÷ 2 = **5% per half-year**.

⇒ Total periods (n) = 1 year × 2 = **2 half-years**.

⇒ A = 72,000 × (1 + 5/100)²

⇒ A = 72,000 × (105/100) × (105/100)

⇒ A = 72,000 × (21/20) × (21/20)

⇒ A = (72,000 ÷ 400) × 441

⇒ A = 180 × 441

⇒ A = ₹79,380

**∴ The correct answer is ₹79,380.**

Compounding Frequency Rules

For **Half-yearly** compounding, Rate = R/2 and Time = 2T. For **Quarterly** compounding, Rate = R/4 and Time = 4T.

Effective Rate Formula

Effective Rate for 2 periods = x + y + (xy/100)%, where x and y are the rates for each period.

CI vs SI Difference

The difference between CI and SI for 2 years (or 2 periods) is given by D = P(r/100)².

questions.question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of ∠R and ∠S meet at point T (inside the quadrilateral) and ∠STR = 32.5°. If the ratio of ∠P to ∠Q is 4 : 9, then what is the difference between the measures of ∠Q and ∠P?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a **quadrilateral**, the angle formed by the **bisectors** of two adjacent angles is half the sum of the other two angles.

⇒ ∠STR = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2

⇒ 32.5° = (∠P + ∠Q) ÷ 2 ⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 65°

⇒ Ratio ∠P : ∠Q = 4 : 9 ⇒ Total units = 13

⇒ 13 units = 65° ⇒ 1 unit = 5°

⇒ Difference = (9 − 4) × 5° = 25°

**∴ The correct answer is 25°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠STR = 32.5°, Ratio of ∠P to ∠Q = 4 : 9.

**Formula Used:** Sum of interior angles of a **quadrilateral** = 360°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/77275850ebcb689b901e884cde54cf6bb3482071cc281efdef2b75b9711a2c36.png] 

⇒ In ΔSTR, ∠TSR + ∠TRS + ∠STR = 180°

⇒ Since ST and RT are **angle bisectors**, ∠TSR = ∠S/2 and ∠TRS = ∠R/2

⇒ (∠S/2) + (∠R/2) + 32.5° = 180°

⇒ (∠S + ∠R) ÷ 2 = 180° − 32.5° = 147.5°

⇒ ∠S + ∠R = 295°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + 295° = 360° ⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 65°

⇒ Let ∠P = 4x and ∠Q = 9x

⇒ 4x + 9x = 65° ⇒ 13x = 65° ⇒ x = 5°

⇒ Difference = 9x − 4x = 5x = 5 × 5° = 25°

**∴ The correct answer is 25°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle Bisector Property in Quadrilaterals

The angle between the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the sum of the remaining two angles.

Sum of Interior Angles

For any polygon with n sides, the sum of interior angles is (n − 2) × 180°. For a quadrilateral (n=4), the sum is 360°.

Ratio and Difference

If two quantities are in ratio a : b and their sum is S, the difference between them is |a − b| × [S ÷ (a + b)].</p

questions.question: What happens to magnetic fields when a material becomes superconducting and experiences the Meissner effect?

options.text: Magnetic fields are completely expelled from the interior of the material.
Magnetic fields penetrate the material freely.
Magnetic fields are increased in strength within the material.
Magnetic fields are absorbed and stored inside the material.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnetic fields are completely expelled from the interior of the material.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Meissner effect is a defining property of superconductors where magnetic fields are expelled from the interior of the material during the transition to the superconducting state.
 
• This phenomenon occurs below a critical temperature (Tc) unique to each superconducting material.
 
• The expulsion of magnetic fields is a result of the superconducting material forming perfect diamagnetic properties.
 
• As the superconducting state is achieved, the material cancels the internal magnetic field by generating surface currents that oppose the applied magnetic field.
 
• It is distinct from perfect conductivity, as it implies both zero electrical resistance and zero magnetic field within the material.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Superconductivity:**

 
 
• Superconductivity is a quantum mechanical phenomenon where certain materials exhibit zero electrical resistance and expel magnetic fields below a critical temperature.
 
• It was discovered in 1911 by Heike Kamerlingh Onnes in mercury cooled to 4.2 K.
 
• Applications include MRI machines, particle accelerators, and quantum computing.
 
 
 
• **Meissner Effect:**
 
 
• Named after Walther Meissner and Robert Ochsenfeld, who discovered it in 1933.
 
• It demonstrates the fundamental difference between superconductors and perfect conductors.
 
• The magnetic field is expelled entirely from the bulk of the material, not just reduced.
 
 
 
• **Type I vs Type II Superconductors:**
 
 
• Type I superconductors completely expel magnetic fields and are typically elemental metals.
 
• Type II superconductors allow partial penetration of magnetic fields in the form of vortices and are often alloys or compounds.
 
 
 
• **Critical Temperature (Tc):**
 
 
• The temperature below which a material becomes superconducting.
 
• Varies widely among materials, from below 1 K in some metals to above 100 K in high-temperature superconductors.

questions.question: When were the Municipal Corporations of Calcutta and Bombay established?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1726**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Municipal Corporations of Calcutta (now Kolkata) and Bombay (now Mumbai) were established in the year **1726**.
 
• They were formed under the provisions of the **Charter of 1726**, issued by the British East India Company.
 
• This Charter led to the establishment of a **Mayor's Court** and municipal governance systems in these cities.
 
• The primary objective was to improve urban administration and cater to the needs of a growing British population in these trading hubs.
 
• These were among the earliest attempts at formal municipal governance in India during the colonial period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Charter of 1726:**

 
 
• It was issued by King George I of Britain at the request of the British East India Company.
 
• The Charter introduced a system of civil and criminal courts in the presidency towns of Bombay, Calcutta, and Madras.
 
• This laid the foundation for modern municipal governance in India.
 
 
 
• **Municipal Governance in Colonial India:**
 
 
• The British introduced municipal governance to ensure better administration, sanitation, and urban development in growing cities.
 
• Municipal corporations were primarily established in trading centers like Bombay, Madras, and Calcutta.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Urban Local Bodies:**
 
 
• The Indian Councils Act of 1861 and 1882 further developed local self-governance in India.
 
• In 1882, Lord Ripon, known as the “Father of Local Self-Government in India,” introduced reforms to make municipal bodies more representative.
 
 
 
• **Current Status:**
 
 
• Today, municipal corporations in India operate under the provisions of the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act (1992).
 
• This amendment provides constitutional status to Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) for decentralized governance.

questions.question: 'The Flying Apsara' painting is a masterpiece in which of the following caves?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **'The Flying Apsara'** is a famous painting located in the **Ajanta Caves**, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Maharashtra, India.
 
• Ajanta Caves are renowned for their exquisite **Buddhist rock-cut architecture** and paintings depicting Jataka tales and the life of Buddha.
 
• 'The Flying Apsara' painting showcases the **elegance and intricate artistry** of ancient Indian painters, emphasizing movement and grace.
 
• The Ajanta frescoes are painted using the **tempera technique**, combining natural pigments and plant-based adhesives to create enduring artworks.
 
• The caves date back to **2nd century BCE to 6th century CE**, representing one of the finest examples of Indian classical art traditions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ajanta Caves:**

 
 
• The Ajanta Caves consist of 30 caves, including monasteries and prayer halls, carved into the rock face of a horseshoe-shaped cliff.
 
• The caves are primarily dedicated to **Buddhism** and were used by monks for meditation and teaching.
 
• They are an important cultural and historical site, preserving ancient Indian art, architecture, and religious practices.
 
 
 
• **Artistic Techniques:**
 
 
• The tempera technique used in Ajanta paintings involves mixing pigments with a binding agent such as gum or egg yolk.
 
• The artists employed natural light in the caves, which filtered through openings, to work on the intricate details.
 
• The paintings depict themes like **Buddhist myths, deities, and daily life activities**, showcasing the harmony between religion and art.
 
 
 
• **Apsaras in Indian Art:**
 
 
• Apsaras are celestial maidens or dancers in Indian mythology, often associated with grace, beauty, and divine energy.
 
• 'The Flying Apsara' painting symbolizes the **dynamic movement and ethereal presence** of these celestial beings.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Status:**
 
 
• The Ajanta Caves were designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **1983**.
 
• They are recognized for their historical importance and artistic achievement, drawing visitors and scholars from around the world.

questions.question: Ravi travels from City A to City B. If Ravi drives his car at (2)/(7) of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 30 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Ravi would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio = 2 : 7 (New : Normal)

Since distance is constant, Time ratio = 7 : 2 (New : Normal)

Difference in time units = 7 − 2 = 5 units

5 units = 30 minutes ⇒ 1 unit = 6 minutes

Normal time = 2 units = 2 × 6 = 12 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 12 minutes.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** New speed = 2/7 of Normal speed, Time delay = 30 minutes.

**Formula Used:** Distance = Speed × Time; If Speed ratio is a : b, then Time ratio is b : a for a fixed distance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3de71664811bdba431341d17b4c3eb6490dcff57235320252f540bffb3f299f4.png] 

⇒ Let normal speed be S and normal time be T.

⇒ New speed = (2/7)S

⇒ New time = T + 30

⇒ S × T = (2/7)S × (T + 30)

⇒ T = (2/7) × (T + 30)

⇒ 7T = 2T + 60

⇒ 5T = 60

⇒ T = 12 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 12 minutes.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When the distance traveled is constant, the speed is inversely proportional to the time taken (S ∝ 1/T).

Average Speed

If a person travels two equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed is given by 2xy/(x + y).

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. For opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.</p

questions.question: What is the temperature of the triple point of water on the Celsius scale?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.01ºC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The triple point of water is the temperature and pressure at which water exists simultaneously in its **solid, liquid, and gaseous states**.
 
• On the Celsius scale, the triple point of water is precisely **0.01ºC**.
 
• This value is used as a standard fixed point in the definition of the Celsius temperature scale.
 
• The corresponding pressure at the triple point of water is exactly **611.657 pascals (Pa)**.
 
• The triple point of water is critical for scientific calibration of thermometers and maintaining the International Temperature Scale.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Triple Point:**

 
 
• The triple point is a unique thermodynamic state where three phases (solid, liquid, and gas) coexist in equilibrium.
 
• It is a fundamental reference point for thermodynamic measurements.
 
 
 
• **Kelvin and Celsius Relationship:**
 
 
• The triple point of water is defined as 273.16 K on the Kelvin scale.
 
• The Celsius scale is defined such that the triple point of water is 0.01ºC.
 
 
 
• **Role in Metrology:**
 
 
• The triple point of water is used in metrology to calibrate temperature-measuring instruments.
 
• It is a key reference point for defining the International Temperature Scale (ITS-90).
 
 
 
• **Physical Significance:**
 
 
• The triple point demonstrates the delicate balance of thermodynamic states under specific conditions.
 
• For water, it highlights the unique properties of this universal solvent, which is critical for life on Earth.

questions.question: What happens when you press Ctrl + S while working on a document in computer system?

__
 
• Pressing **Ctrl + S** in most computer applications is the universal shortcut for saving the current document or file.

• For example, **Ctrl + C** is used to copy, **Ctrl + V** to paste, and **Ctrl + Z** to undo the last action.
 
• These shortcuts help improve productivity and reduce reliance on mouse clicks.
 
 
 
• **Save vs Save As:**
 
 
• The **Save** command updates the current file with any changes made, while **Save As** allows saving the file under a new name or in a different location.
 
• Save As is particularly useful when creating multiple versions of a document.

questions.question: A cylinder is made by rolling a rectangular paper along its breadth. Find the curved surface area of the cylinder, if the length and breadth of the rectangle are 12 m and 7.48 m, respectively. (Use π = (22)/(7))
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a **rectangular paper** is rolled into a **cylinder**, its **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** is exactly equal to the **Area of the Rectangle**.

Area of Rectangle = **Length × Breadth**

Area = 12 m × 7.48 m = 89.76 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 89.76 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length** of rectangular paper (L) = 12 m

**Breadth** of rectangular paper (B) = 7.48 m

The paper is rolled along its **breadth** to form a **cylinder**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b798c71161547ce16410da5c9ba83eec8c3d536304d2fd5f4c37cdae081d8de.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

When rolled along the **breadth**:

⇒ **Height** (h) of cylinder = **Length** of rectangle = 12 m

⇒ **Circumference** (2πr) of base = **Breadth** of rectangle = 7.48 m

**Calculations:**

⇒ CSA = (2πr) × h

⇒ CSA = 7.48 × 12

⇒ CSA = 89.76 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 89.76 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rolling along Length vs Breadth

If rolled along **Length**, h = Breadth and 2πr = Length. If rolled along **Breadth**, h = Length and 2πr = Breadth. In both cases, **CSA** remains the **Area** of the paper.

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

**TSA** = 2πr(h + r). This includes the **CSA** plus the areas of the two circular **bases** (2 × πr²).

Volume of Cylinder

**Volume** = πr²h. It measures the total capacity or **space** occupied by the 3D cylinder.</p
